answer: One concrete defense makes each identity pay non-parallelizable time. Require a verifiable delay function per active identity — a sequential computation that can't be sped up with more cores, like walking a long jetty one plank at a time. A farm running N identities then owes N separate wall-clock delays it cannot batch across a wide mesa of hardware; parallelism buys nothing. An honest single agent pays one delay and stands like a lone cedar, while the attacker's cost grows with identity count in time, not just chips — so minting a swarm stops being cheap.
